findings.english_quote: you bold and utterly rash man
findings.issue: The explicit comparison with everyone else, πάντων, is lost. “Utterly rash” expresses intensity but not the source’s claim that Simon's interlocutor is the rashest of all.
findings.suggested_revision: Use “you bold man, most reckless of all” or “you bold and rashest of all men.” Submit the revised wording for fresh review.

findings.source_quote: τοὺς πατέρα νομίζοντας εἶναι χριστοῦ τὸν Δαυὶδ — καὶ αὐτὸν δὲ τὸν χριστὸν υἱὸν ὄντα — καὶ υἱὸν θεοῦ μὴ ἐγνωκέναι.
findings.english_quote: who supposed David to be the Messiah’s father and did not recognize the Messiah himself as Son and as Son of God.
findings.issue: The draft places both “as Son” and “as Son of God” within the failure to recognize. The printed parenthesis can instead continue the Davidic father–son understanding, or parenthetically affirm the Messiah’s sonship, with the failure to recognize applying specifically to “Son of God.” This materially different attachment is not discussed in the notes.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare the draft explicitly with “who supposed David to be the Messiah’s father—with the Messiah himself being the son—and had not recognized him as Son of God.” Preserve the alternative attachment and explain the chosen scope of μὴ ἐγνωκέναι. If retaining the draft’s attachment, explain its grammatical and contextual basis rather than presenting it as unambiguous.

findings.source_quote: οὐδὲ Ἐνὼχ ὁ εὐαρεστήσας μὴ εἰδέναι οὔτε Νῶε ὁ δίκαιος μὴ ἐπίστασθαι οὔτε Ἀβραὰμ ὁ φίλος μὴ συνιέναι
findings.english_quote: for Enoch, who pleased him, not to have been without knowledge; for righteous Noah not to have been without understanding; for Abraham the friend not to have failed to comprehend;
findings.issue: The treatment of the coordinated negatives and the governing δύναται needs disclosure. These English clauses read as positive possibilities under “it is possible,” whereas the later “nor ... not” clauses can read as excluding the possibility of ignorance. The Greek uses οὐδέ/οὔτε together with μή here too. The existing note addresses the final clause, not this variation in modal and negative scope.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a note explaining how δύναται and the coordinated negatives scope across the entire list. Compare a consistently explicit construction such as “nor can Enoch ... fail to know; nor can righteous Noah ... fail to know; nor can Abraham ... fail to comprehend” with a reading that coordinates the negative infinitival complements. A chosen contextual reading may remain, but its materially different alternative must be preserved.

findings.source_quote: καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐν τῷ λαῷ ἀξίοις μὴ ἀποκεκαλύφθαι.
findings.english_quote: nor for him to have remained unrevealed to all the worthy among the people.
findings.issue: The English opening quotation for Peter’s speech is never closed. The internal quotations are closed, but the passage-level speech quotation is not.
findings.suggested_revision: Add the closing double quotation mark after the final sentence.

findings.source_quote: εἰ δὲ (ὡς φῄς) ἔσται διὰ τὸ εἰδέναι διὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ νῦν πᾶσιν ἀποκαλύπτεσθαι:
findings.english_quote: But if, as you say, it is now through Jesus that he is revealed to everyone for knowledge,
findings.issue: The present-tense English does not represent the future force of ἔσται. It also selects a purposive interpretation of διὰ τὸ εἰδέναι without explaining its attachment or preserving the causal alternative. The difficult construction is not, merely for being difficult, evidence of an OCR defect.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain “will be” or “is to be,” while preserving νῦν as “now.” Explain whether διὰ τὸ εἰδέναι means “because of knowing” or “for the sake of knowing,” and how it relates to ἀποκαλύπτεσθαι. A candidate requiring fresh review is “But if, as you say, he is to be revealed to everyone now through Jesus for the sake of knowing him ...,” accompanied by the causal alternative and an explanation of the supplied object.

findings.source_quote: οὗτοι παντὸς κρείττονος γνῶναι οὐ κατηξιώθησαν;
findings.english_quote: Were those men not deemed worthy to know the one better than all?
findings.issue: The definite personal rendering “the one better than all” is contextually defensible, but it fixes an undisclosed interpretation of παντὸς κρείττονος. Taking παντός with substantival κρείττονος, rather than as the comparative’s complement, permits the more general “anything superior.” The genitive construction also needs explanation in relation to κατηξιώθησαν.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-quoted note preserving “Were these not deemed worthy to know anything superior?” as an alternative and explaining why the context favors a personal referent superior to all. This ordinary ambiguity does not itself require blocking the passage.

findings.issue: This surviving phrase is omitted. The draft correctly acknowledges the omission and retains a blocking verdict in its source issue, but that disclosure does not establish coverage or supply a defensible translation. The supplied transcription is identified as independently image-checked, so the unresolved problem is the meaning of the confirmed printed construction, not an established OCR error or a printed lacuna.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep publication blocked until a defensible analysis of the supplied construction can support English wording. Update the source issue to distinguish the verified printed reading from the unresolved meaning. Any proposed textual correction must quote the supplied reading, identify the correction explicitly as conjectural, and must not silently replace the selected edition. Do not substitute invented dots or an unsupported completion.
